about: Web Push message encryption (RFC 8291, over RFC 8188's aes128gcm): RFC 8291's example (§5) with Appendix A's intermediate values, base64url, taken from the RFC's text. Its body is 144 bytes (§5 says Content-Length 145, a known erratum: 86 of header, 41 of message, the delimiter, the 16-byte tag). A device encrypts a notice to a phone (from the sender's key and the salt, the body); the phone decrypts it (from its own key and secret, the message). `refused`: bodies the phone of that example refuses though they decrypt, each a notice is not (spec/push.md: one record, the last, from an uncompressed key); made apart from the code with node:crypto, from the example's keys and the salt 0x5a × 16.

refused.about: its one record says another follows (delimiter 1): the message was cut short
more than one record: its record is longer than the record size it gives (18)
the sender's key compressed (33 bytes), the record keyed with it as given: RFC 8291 §4 has the key uncompressed, 65 bytes

sender.about:
A device signs each notice it posts to a push server (spec/push.md 0.3, "Sending"): Hive-Sender is its key, the time (ms) and Ed25519 over `hive/push-notice/1
`, the phone's handle (the last segment of the endpoint's path), `
`, the time in decimal, `
` and SHA-256 of the body. RFC 8032's first test key (its seed here) signs rfc8291.body to the phone of `handle` at the time given; made apart from the code with node:crypto.
